summary: R3 completeness review of WP-SCP-023 023B at HEAD commit 24c8992 (fix-round-2 applied). R3 fixpoint reached: 0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ on the completeness/governance lens. Three verification tasks confirmed: (1) CG-R2-MIN-002 CLOSED — docs/releases/v1.2.0.md 'Workflow permissions delta' section (lines 37–40) now reads 'The reusable workflow gains a new `attest-scorecard` job that declares `attestations: write` + `id-token: write` at JOB level (NOT workflow default level). This job is gated on `if: inputs.scorecard-emit` AND `needs: policy-check`, so opt-out runs never get the OIDC permissions granted at all. Workflow-level permissions remain `contents: read` + `statuses: write` — unchanged from prior versions.' This matches the R2 mitigation wording exactly and replaces the stale workflow-level phrasing that CG-R2-MIN-002 flagged. (2) warn-baseline fixture appropriately documented and WARN_BASELINE_RULES traceability confirmed — tests/scorecard-emit/fixtures/warn-baseline/ pair is present (policy-check-summary.json: SCP-R-004 deny finding, no waivers; expected-scorecard-emit.json: verdict='warn', denies=0, raw_findings=1). FIX-ROUND-2.md edit #3 documents the fixture. In the workflow, the emitter heredoc declares WARN_BASELINE_RULES = {"SCP-R-004"} at line 1309 with an inline comment at lines 1303–1308 that reads 'Mirrors the WARN_BASELINE_RULES set in the workflow's render-deny step. Future warn-baseline rules add to this set (or promote to data-driven manifest per TF-020P-001).' The render-deny step's parallel set lives at line 973 with its own comment explaining the set's semantics. The linkage between the two occurrences is explicit and traceable via inline comment and TF-020P-001. (3) No new CRIT or MAJ completeness findings emerge from the fix-round-2 deltas. One nit is raised: docs/releases/v1.2.0.md line 67 still reads '3 fixture pairs' but fix-round-2 added a 4th (warn-baseline/), making the count stale by one. The normative test record (directory + FIX-ROUND-2.md) is authoritative; the release-note count is informational only.
